page.layout: Two medallion woodcut portraits with their legends at top centre, below the running head. Below them one column of text running full width, with no marginal notes and no notes under the text.

main_text.l: FLAVAL. CONSTANTIVS NOB. CAE.
HELENA AVGVSTA CON·MA·AV[?]
CONSTANTIVS Chlorus & Galerius Maximinus fi-
[?]tue Maximianus,ambo à Diocletiano & Maximiano Herculio,
priusquâ se imperio abdicarent,Cæsares facti ac adoptati sunt,
propter varia bella in diuersis locis pullulantia. Constátius na-
tus patre Eutropio, qui genus ab Ænea deducebat, & matre
Claudia,Claudii Augusti filia,Galliis,Hispaniis, Italiæ & Afri-
cæ præfuit:Galerius Illyrico,Græciæ & Orieti. At verò hac di-
uisione Imperii facta,Constantius natura mitis, & diuitiarum
spretor,Italiæ & Africæ Imperiū recusat, quòd putaret ab vno
tantū pōdus minimè sustineri posse:in Galliis & Hispaniis tan-
tùm regnat,propensus ad promerendā Gallorum gratiam,nec
à vera pietate abhorres.Vxores habuit duas,prior fuit Helena,
ex qua Constantinū magnum suscepit:posterior fuit Theodo-
ra,priuigna Maximiani Herculii: quā dimissā Helena, coactus
est ducere. obiit Constantius Eboraci, quod est oppidū in Bri-
tannia, anno 2. postquam Imperio se Diocletianus abdicauit:
nam longè antea Cæsar factus,& à Diocletiano adoptatus fue-
rat.duos igitur veri Imperii annos Constátio tribuo,ab ipsa ab-
dicatione Imperii à Diocletiano,quæ facta est an. mun. 4 2 6
9. à Christo nato 3 0 7. hoc regnante nulli motus in suis ditioni-
bus extitere, hostes popu. Rom. ab armis cessauere. Dictus est
Chlorus,à colore,quasi virens.Vide Pom.Læ.Egna.li.1.
HELENA, prior uxor Constantii,ac magni Constantini
mater,annos nata 80.divinitus monita,Ierusalē perrexit: cru-
cem in qua Christus pendit, non sine labore reperit: Romæ
diem obiit,superstite filio, Deo hominibúsq; gratissima,anno
mundi 4 2 8 6. à Christo nato 3 2 4. Vide Eusc. lib. 10. cap. 7.
& Supple.Chro.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed inside the woodcut illustrations; the right-hand legend's final letters ("CON·MA·AV") are hard to read and are marked [?]. The word "fi-" at the line end of the first paragraph is uncertain (probably the start of "siue"), so it is marked [?]. The printed "Eusebius" abbreviation reads "Eufe." in the scan; it is transcribed as "Eusc." only if that is the correct reading, so treat "Eusc." with caution. The printed "Vide Eusc." may be a misreading of "Eufe." Printed spellings such as "Constátius", "Imperiū" and "pōdus" are kept as printed.
